title: Write a Tree as One Line of Text

concept.title: Pre-order plus a mark for every missing child
body: *Serialization* turns a structure into text from which it can be rebuilt exactly. For a binary tree a pre-order walk is not enough (many trees have the same pre-order list), but if you also write a **mark for every missing child**, the text is unambiguous. Use `#` for a missing child and write the values and marks separated by commas: the tree `1` with the children `2` and `3` becomes `1,2,#,#,3,#,#`.

body.code:
def serialize(root, out):
    if root is None:
        out.append("#")                    # a missing child
        return
    out.append(str(root.val))
    serialize(root.left, out)
    serialize(root.right, out)

# print(",".join(out))

body: Why is it enough? When the text is read from the left, a value means "a node, then its left subtree, then its right subtree", and a `#` means "an empty tree here", so the structure can be followed without any other information (the next problem rebuilds a tree from such a text). A tree with `n` nodes gives `2n + 1` words: `n` values and `n + 1` marks.

statement: Write a binary tree as one line of text: do a pre-order walk, write the value of every node and a `#` for every missing child, and join all the words with commas (no spaces).
inputFormat: The first line has `t`, the number of words in the description of the tree.
The second line has the tree in level order: the root first, then the children of the nodes row by row from left to right. `N` stands for a missing child. There is no `N` at the end.
constraints: The height of the tree is at most 800.

examples.note: The root 1, the left child 2 with two missing children, the right child 3 with two missing children: 1,2,#,#,3,#,#.

hints: Walk the tree in pre-order: the node first, then the left subtree, then the right subtree.
Collect the words in a list and join them with commas at the end.

starter.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right


# Builds a binary tree from a level-order list of words; "N" marks a missing child.
def build_tree(vals):
    if not vals or vals[0] == "N":
        return None
    root = TreeNode(int(vals[0]))
    queue = [root]
    head = 0
    i = 1
    while head < len(queue) and i < len(vals):
        node = queue[head]
        head += 1
        if vals[i] != "N":
            node.left = TreeNode(int(vals[i]))
            queue.append(node.left)
        i += 1
        if i < len(vals) and vals[i] != "N":
            node.right = TreeNode(int(vals[i]))
            queue.append(node.right)
        i += 1
    return root


# Prints a tree in the same level-order form ("empty" for no tree).
def print_tree(root):
    if root is None:
        print("empty")
        return
    out = []
    queue = [root]
    head = 0
    while head < len(queue):
        node = queue[head]
        head += 1
        if node is None:
            out.append("N")
        else:
            out.append(str(node.val))
            queue.append(node.left)
            queue.append(node.right)
    while out and out[-1] == "N":
        out.pop()
    print(" ".join(out))

t = int(input())

solution.complexity: Time O(n), space O(h) besides the output.
